findings.title: Reminder mailed twice: directly and again by the consumer
findings.detail: send_reminders mails the member itself and then transition() publishes loan.reminded. The consumer mails again on every loan.reminded event.
findings.suggestion: Make the event the only trigger: send_reminders should only transition and publish, and the consumer should do the mailing.
findings.effect: Each member gets two reminder emails per due loan.
preconditions: the queue is consumed by library.consumer
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: publish_overdue always raises ValueError
findings.detail: It selects loans with due_on == day - 1 and calls transition(loan, OVERDUE, ...). status_of(loan, day) already returns OVERDUE for those loans because due_on < day. move(OVERDUE, OVERDUE) is not in MOVES, so it raises. It also never marks the loan, so a second run would try again.
findings.suggestion: Allow the derived-OVERDUE to OVERDUE move, or persist the status or an overdue_on field and check it. Add a test.
findings.effect: No loan.overdue event is ever published, and the first late loan aborts the whole batch.
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: /remind bypasses the state machine and has no input or error handling
findings.detail: It calls consumer.handle directly. That mails without transition() or move(), so it ignores the state machine: a returned loan is mailed anyway, and repeat calls re-mail. It also publishes no event. It ignores the HTTP method. A missing 'id' (KeyError), invalid JSON, or an unknown loan id (KeyError in store.get) raises an unhandled exception. The route returns 202 although the work was done synchronously. It also contradicts transition()'s docstring, 'the only place a status changes'.
findings.suggestion: Validate the input, return 400 or 404, and call transition(loan, REMINDED, queue, today()) so the event is published and the consumer does the mailing.
findings.effect: A front-desk caller gets a 500 or a duplicate mail to a member whose loan is already returned. Loan state diverges from the events.
preconditions: an authenticated caller posts /remind with a bad, unknown or returned loan id
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: Consumer reads from an in-memory store the front desk does not share
findings.detail: The consumer looks the loan up in api.store, an in-process LoanStore. The consumer and the front desk are separate Lambdas, so the consumer's store is empty. The lookup raises KeyError, and every message fails and is retried. The consumer's loan.reminded_on = today() also changes a copy nobody else sees.
findings.suggestion: Back the store with a shared database, or put the recipient and book in the event payload.
findings.effect: In the deployed consumer Lambda no reminder or overdue mail is ever sent.
preconditions: the consumer is deployed as its own Lambda per template.yaml
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: No SQS publisher: the production queue is never written
findings.detail: Queue only appends to a list, though its docstring says SQS in production. template.yaml passes LOAN_EVENTS_URL and the SQS policy, but no code reads the variable or calls SQS. The handler never passes a queue to transition either.
findings.suggestion: Add an SQS-backed Queue that reads LOAN_EVENTS_URL, and wire it in at the entry points.
findings.effect: In production events never reach the SQS queue, so the consumer never runs.
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: Non-idempotent consumer, and one failing record retries the whole batch
findings.detail: handle() has no dedupe, such as checking reminded_on or the loan status. SQS delivers at least once, so a redelivery mails again. Any exception in the loop fails the whole batch of 10, and the records already mailed are retried. template.yaml sets no ReportBatchItemFailures and no dead-letter queue. The loan.returned event type is silently ignored.
findings.suggestion: Skip already-handled events, return batchItemFailures per record, and add a redrive policy.
findings.effect: Members get duplicate emails, and a poison message blocks its batch indefinitely.
preconditions: SQS redelivery, or one bad record in a batch
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: transition is not the only place status changes; loan.returned is never published
findings.detail: LoanStore.give_back (loans.py:41) and api.give_back set returned_on directly and never call transition(RETURNED). The loan.returned event is defined but nothing publishes it, and the move guard is skipped. The docstring claim 'The only place a status changes' is false.
findings.suggestion: Route give_back through transition, with the queue injected.
findings.effect: Returns publish no event and are not checked against the state machine.
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: Mail is sent before the state change and event, with no atomicity
findings.detail: mailer.send runs before transition. If transition raises (an invalid move) or publish fails, the mail has gone out but reminded_on may be unset or the event lost. The next run re-mails. transition also mutates the loan before publish, so a publish failure leaves the loan changed with no event. Mailer.send also swallows failures: after 3 retries it returns without raising.
findings.suggestion: Publish first, or make the order explicit and idempotent. Have Mailer.send raise after the final retry.
findings.effect: Duplicate mails, or a loan marked reminded without an event or mail.
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: Function timeout and queue visibility timeout are mismatched
findings.detail: Timeout is 10s for the consumer, which processes batches of 10 with Mailer retries that sleep 1+2+4s. The SQS queue uses the default 30s visibility timeout. SAM requires the queue's visibility timeout to be at least the function timeout, and it sets no dead-letter queue. The FrontDesk also has no CodeUri, and the HttpApi has no explicit routes.
findings.suggestion: Raise the consumer's timeout, set VisibilityTimeout to at least 6 times the timeout, and add a DLQ.
findings.effect: Batches time out mid-way and are redelivered, which sends duplicate mails.
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: New behavior is untested
findings.detail: There is no test for publish_overdue, which would have exposed the ValueError. There is no test for /remind in handler.py. There is no test for the consumer's overdue branch. The reminder test does not check that an event is published or that exactly one mail is sent end to end.
findings.suggestion: Add tests for publish_overdue, /remind, the consumer overdue path, and a combined send_reminders plus consumer flow.
findings.effect: The double-mail and overdue bugs ship without any failing test.
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: Empty default token lets `Authorization: Bearer ` through
findings.detail:
`TOKEN` defaults to `""`, and `template.yaml` never sets `FRONT_DESK_TOKEN`. A request with the header `Bearer ` (empty token) passes `startswith("Bearer ")`, and `hmac.compare_digest("", "")` is true.

The check therefore fails open, and `/remind` and `/late` are open to anyone on the internet.
findings.effect: Anyone on the internet can trigger reminder mails to members and read the overdue list, which holds member names.
preconditions: FRONT_DESK_TOKEN is unset or empty in the deployment (the template does not set it)
The HttpApi route has no authorizer (none in template.yaml)
findings.path_why: assumed: depends on the deployment leaving FRONT_DESK_TOKEN empty and the API gateway passing the header through
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: Queue.publish only appends to a list, never sends to SQS
findings.detail:
`Queue.publish` appends to an in-memory list. Nothing calls SQS `send_message`, and `LOAN_EVENTS_URL` is never read.

The `SQSSendMessagePolicy` grant on `FrontDesk` is unused and the `ReminderConsumer` trigger never receives an event. The whole event path, e5 and e6, is dead in production.
findings.suggestion: Implement an SQS-backed `Queue` that calls `send_message` with `LOAN_EVENTS_URL`, and use it in the Lambdas.
findings.effect: loan.reminded and loan.overdue events never leave the front desk Lambda, so members get no reminders from the queue path.
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: Consumer reads loans from a per-process in-memory store
findings.detail:
`api.store` is a `LoanStore` dict that lives in each Lambda container's memory. The `ReminderConsumer` is a separate function with its own empty store, so `api.store.get(loan_id)` raises `KeyError` for every message.

The front desk's own store is also lost on each cold start, and it is not shared between concurrent instances.
findings.suggestion: Back `LoanStore` with a shared database such as DynamoDB.
findings.effect: Every queued event fails in the consumer, and the loan data is lost whenever a Lambda container is recycled.
preconditions: The consumer runs as its own Lambda (template.yaml:28)
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: One failing record re-runs the whole batch; no DLQ, no idempotency
findings.detail:
`handler` loops over up to 10 records, and any exception, such as the `KeyError` for an unknown loan or malformed JSON, fails the whole batch. SQS then redelivers all 10 messages, so members whose mails already went out get them again. The queue has no `RedrivePolicy` or DLQ, so a poison message is retried until retention expires.

The handler also does not return `batchItemFailures`, and there is no dedupe on `reminded_on`.
findings.suggestion: Enable `ReportBatchItemFailures` and return the failed ids, add a DLQ, and skip loans that were already reminded.
findings.effect: Members receive duplicate reminder mails, and one bad message blocks the other messages in its batch.
preconditions: The queue is wired to a real SQS publisher
A batch contains a record that raises
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: /remind sends mail with no validation, state check or dedupe
findings.detail:
`/remind` takes `id` from the body without validation. It then calls `consumer.handle` directly, which skips `transition` and the `due_soon` and `reminded_on` checks. A missing `id`, bad JSON or an unknown loan raises, so the caller gets a 500.

Returned or already-reminded loans are mailed again on every call, and a `loan.returned` or bad `type` is not handled. The handler sets `reminded_on` directly and publishes no event.
findings.suggestion: Look the loan up, require it to be open and not yet reminded, and go through `transition` instead of calling the consumer.
findings.code: # The front desk wants the mail out at once, so skip the queue for this one loan.
findings.effect: A caller holding the token, or anyone if f1 applies, can send repeated mails to any member, including those who already returned the book.
preconditions: The caller is authenticated or f1 holds
findings.path_why: The route is reached by any caller holding the bearer token (or any caller if f1 applies).
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: send_reminders mails directly and also publishes an event the consumer mails again
findings.detail:
`send_reminders` calls `mailer.send` and then `transition(..., REMINDED)`, which publishes `loan.reminded`. The consumer sends the same mail for that event.

Once the queue is wired to SQS, each reminder goes out twice.
findings.suggestion: Remove the direct `mailer.send` and leave the mailing to the consumer.
findings.effect: Members get two identical reminder mails per loan.
preconditions: The queue is wired to SQS (see f2)
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: Nothing runs send_reminders or publish_overdue: no schedule, no entry point
findings.detail:
`send_reminders` and `publish_overdue` are called only from tests. `handler.py` routes only `/remind` and `/late`, and `template.yaml` has no `Schedule` event or third function.

In production no `loan.reminded` or `loan.overdue` event is created by a status change, and the two-days-before mail never goes out unless the front desk posts each loan to `/remind` by hand.
findings.suggestion: Add a scheduled function (an EventBridge `Schedule` event in `template.yaml`) that calls both functions once a day, with an alarm on its errors.
findings.effect: Members get no automatic due-soon or overdue mail, and nobody sees that the job never runs.
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: Mailer swallows an exhausted retry, so /remind answers 202 and the queue deletes the message
findings.detail:
After `RETRIES` failed attempts `Mailer.send` falls out of the loop and returns `None` without raising. It also sleeps 1+2+4 = 7s, and the 4s sleep comes after the last attempt.

The new callers rely on `send` raising to learn the mail failed. `handler.py:21` goes on to answer 202 `reminded: true`, and `consumer.handle` returns, so SQS deletes the message. In both cases the mail is lost with no error and no log above debug.

The 7s of sleeps plus any SMTP timeouts also leave little room in the 10s function timeout (`template.yaml:8`) for the request route. In the consumer, a batch of 10 can reach 70s.
findings.suggestion: Re-raise the last `OSError` after the final attempt and skip the sleep after the last attempt.
findings.effect: A member's reminder is lost while the front desk is told it was sent, and SQS never redelivers it.
preconditions: `Mailer.send` raises `OSError` for a real transport (today it only appends to a list, so the path is not exercised)
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: Date equality windows skip a loan forever if one daily run is missed
findings.detail:
`due_soon` matches only `due_on == day + 2` and `publish_overdue` matches only `due_on == day - 1`.

A missed or failed daily run, a retried run on the next day, or a UTC against local-time day shift in `dates.today()` means the loan never matches again. Its reminder or overdue event is lost with no signal.
findings.suggestion: Select loans with `due_on <= day + 2` (and `reminded_on is None`) so a later run catches up.
findings.code: return [l for l in loans if l.open and l.due_on == day and l.reminded_on is None]
findings.effect: A member whose loan fell on a skipped day never gets the reminder or the overdue notice.
preconditions: The daily job misses a day, or runs near midnight in a timezone other than UTC
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: The consumer and /remind log nothing at info level, and the event has no id
findings.detail:
`handle` sends mail and mutates the loan without a log line. The only trace is `log.debug("mail to %s")` in the mailer, which includes the member's email and is off at the default level.

An event carries no id, no correlation id and no trace context across the publish/consume hop, and nothing alarms on consumer errors. On-call cannot tell which loan was mailed, how often, or which record broke a batch.
findings.suggestion: Log `type`, `loan_id` and the message id at info level in `handle`, and alarm on the consumer's Errors metric.
findings.effect: On-call cannot tell duplicate, lost or failing reminder mails from normal ones.
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb

findings.title: Module-level Mailer only appends to a list: no mail leaves and the list grows in warm Lambdas
findings.detail:
`Mailer()` gets the default in-memory `outbox`. In the consumer and the front desk (which imports `consumer`) every handled event or `/remind` appends the member's email, name and book to a list that is never drained or sent.

No SMTP transport exists in the repo. The list grows for the life of each warm container and holds personal data.
findings.suggestion: Inject a real SMTP or SES-backed mailer into the consumer, and keep the outbox for tests only.
findings.effect: Consumer-sent reminder mails are never delivered, and memory grows with every request.
preconditions: Deployed as is, with no real transport injected
findings.head: ccddf9524aec9c46d338d296bacce38d994af5fb
